name: AIBAST Agents Library (ms-rapp)
what: A catalog of single-file AI agents for the Microsoft AI stack, plus the runtime that executes them. Every surface is a static JSON file: no key, no quota, CORS-open, safe to poll.

conventions.static_api: rapp-static-api/1.0 — the repository is the API; pin a commit SHA in a raw URL for an immutable response.
conventions.agent_format: One file per agent. A __manifest__ dict carries name, version, description, tags, category, requires_env.
conventions.naming: @publisher/slug — the publisher is a GitHub username.

start_here.then: Filter on .category or .tags; each entry carries raw_url.
Fetch .raw_url — it is plain Python, meant to be read before it is run.

start_here.goal: Find agents for a use case
start_here.then: Pick a category id, then filter agents.json by it.
Read .totals; methodology and caveats are documented on the metrics page.
Lowercase the username first. A 404 and certified=false both mean not certified — neither is an error to retry.

start_here.goal: Read how the platform is built and why
start_here.then: Each post carries raw_url for the Markdown, or subscribe to blog/feed.json (JSON Feed 1.1).
Each note carries raw_url; follow .links to traverse the documentation graph, or fetch llms-full.txt for everything inline.

rules_for_agents: Read an agent file before executing it. Single-file design exists so this is cheap.
Never send secrets to this API; it is a public read-only catalog.
Configuration for an agent comes from the environment via requires_env, never from the file.
Treat unknown fields as ignorable — documents gain fields without a major version.
Poll no more than the daily build cadence; nothing here changes faster.
